conflict_topics: strong-smelling cooking (salted fish) vs shared living space
timing of cooking vs Agent A's work calls
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants gave specific, practical information (work hours, laundry nights) that enabled a schedule-based solution: 'I'm on calls... until about 7 p.m.'; 'I do my laundry on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday evenings.'
Resolution was concrete and mutually accepted rather than a vague promise: D proposed exact alternative times and A accepted.
Conversation is concise and cooperative; minimal off-topic or repeated statements.
evaluation.final_reason: Parties agreed a concrete schedule and restrictions: Agent D agreed not to cook salted fish when laundry is hanging (Agent D: '...what if I don't cook it when there is laundry hanging in the service yard?'; Agent C: 'I do my laundry on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday evenings.') and proposed cooking on Tuesday or Thursday evenings after 7 or on weekends (Agent D: '...if I cook on Tuesday or Thursday evenings after 7, or on the weekends, would that work?'), which Agent A accepted (Agent A: 'Yeah, that works for me. Thanks.'). B and C also affirmed the plan. This is a compromise: D retains cooking at some times while avoiding times that clash with others' needs.
position_change_notes: Agent D moved from implicit continuation of a routine (cooking salted fish twice a week) to concrete concessions: not cooking when laundry is hanging and limiting cooking to Tue/Thu after 7 or weekends ('...if I cook on Tuesday or Thursday evenings after 7, or on the weekends...').
Agent A moved from a blanket request ('nobody cook strong-smelling food') to accepting a limited, time-based arrangement ('Yeah, that works for me. Thanks.').
Agents B and C accepted the proposed schedule and laundry accommodation without further contest; no subsequent changes of position were made in the transcript.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'When there are strong cooking smells, they hang around for hours...'; Agent B: 'My room is next to the kitchen. The smell gets into all my clothes.' (A has just asked that nobody cook strong-smelling food in the flat.)

Agent C: 'My laundry is in the service yard. It all smells of fish now.' Agent D: 'It was me, I was cooking salted fish. It's just what I eat at home.' (D admits a recurring practice that directly conflicts with others' interests.)

Agent A: 'Okay, but the smell is a problem for three of us. What can we do about it?' Agent B: 'If I keep my door shut and my window open, the smell doesn't come into my room.' (Problem-solving begins; suggestions offered but D has not agreed to change.)

Agent C: 'The service yard is open. My clothes will still smell.' Agent D: 'Okay, for the laundry... what if I don't cook it when there is laundry hanging in the service yard?' (D offers a concrete change addressing the laundry issue.)

Agent A: 'That helps with the laundry. Thanks for that. But what about the living room? The smell is still the main problem for me when I'm working.' Agent D: 'Okay, when are the times you're working?' (Laundry mostly addressed; living-room/work-time conflict remains.)

Agent A: 'I'm on calls with clients on weekdays, usually until about 7 p.m.' Agent C: 'Okay, that works for me. I do my laundry on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday evenings.' (Schedules provided, narrowing the conflict to timing.)

Agent D: 'Okay. So if I cook on Tuesday or Thursday evenings after 7, or on the weekends, would that work?' Agent A: 'Yeah, that works for me. Thanks.' (D proposes a schedule and A immediately accepts; timing/laundry constraints are settled.)
Agent D: 'Okay, great.' Agent B: 'That's fine with me.' (Agreement affirmed by others; no substantive disagreement expressed.)
Agent C: 'Yes, that works for me.' (All parties have affirmed the schedule; no unresolved substantive conflict present.)

substantive_insights: The main tension was a clash between one person's habitual food practice (salted fish) and others' use of shared airspace for work and laundry.
Time-based coordination (scheduling) is an effective, low-cost solution when physical modifications and money are unavailable.

Resolving one physical pathway of conflict (laundry in the service yard) required a different adjustment (not cooking when laundry is out) than resolving the living-room/work conflict (avoid cooking during calls).
